items.title: Colby Parkinson caught both targets for minus one yard in the Rams’ Week 12 win over the Packers.
items.text: Parkinson somehow lost a yard on two reception despite the team losing both Tyler Higbee and Davis Allen to injury, the latter of whom departed in the first half and the former of whom left at the beginning of the fourth quarter. The Rams completely controlled the flow of the game after Packers receiver Christian Watson departed with a concussion following a vicious targeting hit down the sideline just before the half, eventually leading to 47 total team carries to just 23 Matthew Stafford pass attempts. items.title: Konata Mumpfield caught 4-of-5 targets for 69 yards in the Rams’ Week 12 win over the Packers.
items.text: Mumpfield saw a team-high five targets and turned them into a team-leading 69 yards in one of the more dominant performances of the season. Despite the seemingly close score, the Rams jumped out to an early 13-3 lead while holding the Packers to only 44 total offensive plays run from scrimmage. The inability of the Packers to move the football resulted in additional time of possession for the Rams, which they used to notch 47 rush attempts to just 23 Matthew Stafford pass attempts, eight of which were directed at the backfield duo of Blake Corum and Kyren Williams. items.title: Kyren Williams rushed 12 times for 46 yards and a touchdown in the Rams’ Week 12 win over the Packers, adding 19 yards on four receptions.
items.text: Williams now operates as the clear change of pace option and preferred back in passing situations, with recent reports pointing to consistent pain due to a turf toe injury likely the culprit in the shifting dynamics of the backfield in Los Angeles. Either way, Williams spent most of the second half on the sideline as Corum set career highs in attempts (32) and yards (184) while becoming the first back in the Sean McVay era to reach 30 carries. Given the nature of the injury, this could be the new norm for a Rams team that continues to push for a postseason bid following a 2-4 start to their 20

items.title: Blake Corum rushed 32 times for 184 yards and a touchdown in the Rams’ Week 12 win over the Packers, adding 21 yards on two receptions.
items.text: The 184 yards on the ground easily set a new career high for the veteran back and his 32 carries marked the first time in the Sean McVay era where a single back ran the football 30 or more times, a mark that had not been reached since Todd Gurley over a decade ago. His trip to paint stretched his streak of touchdowns to five games while he also went over 100 yards for the second straight contest. items.title: Matthew Stafford completed 16-of-23 passes for 140 yards and an interception in the Rams’ 26-13, Week 12 win over the Packers.
items.text: The two sides traded blows in the first half as the Packers came from behind to knot the game at 13 heading into the break, with Stafford leading three consecutive scoring drives to start the game for the first time this season. That was also the first time the Packers had allowed an opponent to score on three consecutive drives to start a game this season, but the departure of Christian Watson in the second quarter due to a concussion completely took the wind out of their sails in the second half. items.title: Tucker Kraft caught 3-of-5 targets for 24 yards in the Packers’ Week 12 loss to the Rams.
items.text: Kraft continues to look miles behind where he was during his breakout 2025 season before suffering a torn ACL, lacking burst out of routes while struggling through mental mistakes. Another such mistake appeared against the Rams when Kraft was stripped of the football in the first quarter following his longest reception in the game. The once-imposing Green Bay offense feel completely flat following the departure of Christian Watson in the second quarter due to a concussion, failing to score after the break while running just 44 total offensive plays. items.title: Matthew Golden caught 1-of-5 targets for 39 yards in the Packers’ Week 12 loss to the Rams.
items.text: Golden found himself in lockdown coverage throughout, particularly following the departure of fellow receiver Christian Watson in the second quarter. The talented second-year receiver has seen double-digit targets in six of 11 games in his sophomore campaign and could be headed for another high-target game against the Saints in Week 13, pending Watson’s availability on a long week. Golden would be a legitimate WR1, should Watson miss, and an upside WR2, should Watson play. - Mark Garcia

items.title: Kaleb Johnson rushed eight times for 13 yards in the Packers’ Week 12 loss to the Rams, adding 19 yards on one reception.
items.text: The Packers were completely unable to run the football effectively against the stout Los Angeles defensive front, running just 44 offensive plays as they struggled to get any offense going following the departure of Christian Watson due to a concussion. Lead back Josh Jacobs appeared close to suiting up coming out of their bye and could make his way back into the starting lineup on a long week ahead of a Week 13 meeting with the Saints. - Mark Garcia

items.title: Jordan Love completed 17-of-29 passes for 198 yards, one touchdown, and two interceptions in the Packers’ 26-13, Week 12 loss to the Rams, adding seven yards on one carry.
items.text: it was the second consecutive game with three turnovers for the Packers as two second half interceptions thrown by Love were a microcosm of the team’s inability to hang with the Rams without their top option through the air. Christian Watson departed in the second quarter with a concussion after being knocked out on a vicious hit down the sideline, leaving the Packers in a hole they could not climb out of despite taking a tied game into the break. items.title: Tyler Higbee (chest) was ruled out for the remainder of Week 12 against the Packers.
items.text: It is unknown when Higbee sustained the injury but he was shown walking to the locker room at the start of the fourth quarter, with the broadcast stating that he was ruled out for the remainder of the game. Higbee caught 1-of-3 targets for 14 yards prior to departing, with his absence of particular note considering fellow tight end Davis Allen was already ruled out in the second quarter with an ankle injury. Perhaps rookie Max Klare will see meaningful run in their absences. - Mark Garcia
